subject: humanities
passage: When the first line of the Paris Métro opened in 1900, its street entrances were designed by Hector Guimard, a young architect whose work in the Art Nouveau style had already attracted attention. Guimard's entrances were cast in iron and painted green, with railings that curved like plant stems and lamps held aloft on stalks shaped like the buds of some enormous flower. Although critics at the time found the entrances strange and even unsettling, and dozens were removed in the decades that ______ that remain are now protected as historic monuments. Of the roughly 140 entrances built, fewer than 90 survive.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The third sentence begins with "Although," so everything up to "in the decades that followed" is one long dependent clause containing two parts joined by "and." The main clause is "those that remain are now protected as historic monuments." A dependent clause that comes first is joined to its main clause with a comma.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses, but the "Although" clause is dependent and cannot stand alone.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Without a comma, the long introductory clause runs straight into the main clause, and "that followed those that remain" becomes impossible to read.
explanation.C: Correct. The comma links the introductory "Although" clause to the main clause "those that remain are now protected."
explanation.D: Incorrect. A period would leave "Although critics … in the decades that followed" as a fragment with no main clause.
